Posterior summaries of the reliability profile

Source: R/posterior.R, R/class-reliability-posterior.R
reliability_posterior.Rd

Computes the posterior distribution of the informativeness, the mean reliability, the dispersion and the concentration count of a set of site estimates with standard errors, under the normal hierarchical model, and the posterior means and intervals of the site effects.

Usage

reliability_posterior(
  estimate,
  ...,
  se = NULL,
  se2 = NULL,
  site = NULL,
  data = NULL,
  mean_model = ~1,
  prior = sd_prior("flat"),
  level = 0.95,
  threshold = 0.5,
  scale_label = NULL,
  target_label = NULL,
  na_action = c("fail", "omit"),
  control = posterior_control()
)

# S3 method for class 'reliability_posterior'
format(x, ..., use_cli = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'reliability_posterior'
print(x, ..., use_cli = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'reliability_posterior'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'summary.reliability_posterior'
format(x, ..., use_cli = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'summary.reliability_posterior'
print(x, ..., use_cli = NULL)

# S3 method for class 'reliability_posterior'
update(
  object,
  ...,
  prior = NULL,
  level = NULL,
  threshold = NULL,
  control = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'reliability_posterior'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

estimate

The site estimates: a numeric vector, or a column of data. It can also be a random-effects fit of metafor (rma.uni) or a data set simulated by multisiteDGP, which carry the estimates and their sampling variances (see metafor-methods and multisitedgp-methods).

...

Must be empty. The arguments after estimate are named, because an unnamed vector could hold standard errors or sampling variances.

se, se2

The standard errors of the estimates, or their sampling variances (the squared standard errors): positive numbers, or a column of data. Give one of the two.

site

Optional labels of the sites, all distinct, used in the tables and plots.

data

A data frame in which estimate, se, se2, site and the variables of mean_model are found. A column takes precedence over a variable of the same name in the calling environment; write .env$x for the variable.

mean_model

A one-sided formula for the mean of the effects, as in a meta-regression; ~ 1, the default, is a common mean.

prior

The prior of the between-site standard deviation, made by sd_prior(); flat by default. In update(), NULL keeps the prior of the fit, as it does for level, threshold and control.

level

Probability content of the posterior intervals, a number between 0 and 1.

threshold

The value of the informativeness whose posterior probability of being exceeded is reported, between 0 and 1. See prob_above().

scale_label, target_label

Optional strings that name the scale of the effects, such as "risk difference" (read as "on the risk difference scale"), and the estimand at each site, such as "the block-adjusted intention-to-treat contrast for course passing". They appear in the printed output and in report_text().

na_action

"fail" (the default) stops at a site with a missing value; "omit" leaves such sites out, with a message that names them.

control

Settings of the numerical integration, from posterior_control().

x, object

A fit of reliability_posterior().

use_cli

Whether to print the headings in bold with the cli package, when it is installed. NULL, the default, takes getOption("poolinfo.use_cli", TRUE).

row.names, optional

Ignored.

Value

reliability_posterior() and update() return an object of class reliability_posterior, a list whose main components are

  • summary: a data frame with the posterior mean, standard deviation and interval of each diagnostic, of sigma_tau, sigma_tau^2 and of the mean or the coefficients.

  • quantiles: the lower end, median and upper end of the same quantities.

  • probability: the posterior probability that \(I\) exceeds threshold.

  • plugin: the diagnostics at the posterior mean of sigma_tau^2.

  • sites: the posterior means of the site reliabilities and site effects.

  • checks: the checks of the numerical integration.

  • data, prior, control, level, threshold, labels and call: the inputs.

The accessors profile_summary(), site_table(), prob_above(), plugin_gap(), functional_density(), profile_draws() and check_numerics() return these numbers as data frames and vectors, and plot() shows plot_dashboard(). summary() returns an object that prints the longer summary, and as.data.frame() returns the site table.

Details

The working model is $$\hat\tau_j \mid \tau_j \sim N(\tau_j, v_j), \qquad \tau_j \sim N(x_j^\top\beta, \sigma_\tau^2),$$ independently over sites, with the sampling variances \(v_j\) taken as known. The coefficients \(\beta\) (by default the common mean) have a flat prior and are integrated out, which leaves a posterior for sigma_tau alone (Lee, 2026, Appendix D). The default prior of sigma_tau is flat too, as in Lee (2026). Each summary is a one-dimensional integral over this posterior, computed numerically to about 10 digits, so there is no Monte Carlo error.

The diagnostics are functions of sigma_tau and the \(v_j\). The informativeness \(I\), the mean reliability, the harmonic centroid and the concentration count increase with sigma_tau. The posterior intervals are central, with probability \((1 - \mathrm{level})/2\) below and above them, so for these four quantities they are the images of the interval of sigma_tau. The dispersion \(H\) first rises and then falls, and its quantiles take both branches into account. The logit variance \(V\) depends on the \(v_j\) only and has no posterior distribution.

The summaries are conditional on the supplied standard errors, which are treated as exact, and every site counts the same in them, whatever its size. The last two lines of the printed header state both.

Under the flat prior the posterior is proper with at least \(p + 2\) sites, where \(p\) is the number of columns of the mean model (3 sites for a common mean). The posterior mean of sigma_tau needs at least \(p + 3\) sites and that of sigma_tau^2 at least \(p + 4\). A posterior standard deviation needs the next moment as well: at least \(p + 4\) sites for sigma_tau and the mean, and \(p + 6\) for sigma_tau^2. The posterior mean of the common mean or a mean-model coefficient requires \(E(\sigma_\tau)\) to exist, hence at least \(p + 3\) sites under the flat prior. With fewer sites its mean is not defined, although a central posterior interval is available. Undefined moments are NA, and the printed fit marks them as not defined. sd_prior() gives the conditions under the other priors. The paper's results are for a common mean and the flat prior. Mean models with covariates and proper SD priors are experimental extensions beyond Lee (2026); their interfaces may change in a later 0.x release. vignette("implementation") describes their computation.

References

Lee, J. (2026). The geometry of informativeness: A Bregman-centroid diagnostic for partial pooling in multisite trials. Unpublished manuscript.

See also

reliability_profile() for a profile at a fixed sigma_tau; reliability_draws() for posterior draws from other software; compare_profiles() and prior_sensitivity() for several analyses; vignette("poolinfo") for a worked analysis and vignette("posterior-summaries") for the choices behind the summaries.

Examples

fit <- reliability_posterior(estimate, se = se, site = school, data = eight_schools)
fit
#> Reliability profile of 8 sites (posterior)
#> Model: estimate ~ N(effect, se^2), effect ~ N(mean, sigma_tau^2),
#>        sites independent
#> Prior: flat on the mean and on sigma_tau
#> Summaries are conditional on the supplied standard errors.
#> Each site counts equally in the diagnostics, whatever its size.
#> 
#>                              mean     95% interval
#>   informativeness I          0.225    0.000    0.745
#>   mean reliability           0.230    0.000    0.735
#>   dispersion H               0.0143   0.0000   0.0283
#>   concentration count J_eff  7.2      6.8      7.9      of 8
#>   logit variance V           0.230    (fixed by the standard errors)
#>   sigma_tau                  6.58     0.243    20.8
#>   effect mean                7.93     -2.09    18.2
#> 
#>   Pr(I > 0.5)                0.138
#>   I at E(sigma_tau^2)        0.338
profile_summary(fit)
#>      quantity        mean          sd         lower        upper
#> 1           I  0.22529451   0.2173025  3.997828e-04   0.74517275
#> 2        mean  0.22972844   0.2150459  4.438244e-04   0.73510308
#> 3    harmonic  0.21033305   0.2084266  3.547019e-04   0.72178667
#> 4           H  0.01428773   0.0100617  4.407725e-05   0.02832835
#> 5       J_eff  7.17004472   0.3177007  6.818171e+00   7.86891743
#> 6           V  0.23016500   0.0000000  2.301650e-01   0.23016500
#> 7   sigma_tau  6.57548335   5.6503793  2.426961e-01  20.75245613
#> 8  sigma_tau2 75.16376789 162.2015906  5.890141e-02 430.66443537
#> 9 effect_mean  7.93237502   5.1783948 -2.090220e+00  18.21814307
update(fit, prior = sd_prior("half_normal", scale = 10))
#> Reliability profile of 8 sites (posterior)
#> Model: estimate ~ N(effect, se^2), effect ~ N(mean, sigma_tau^2),
#>        sites independent
#> Prior: half-normal on sigma_tau with scale 10, flat on the mean
#> Summaries are conditional on the supplied standard errors.
#> Each site counts equally in the diagnostics, whatever its size.
#> 
#>                              mean     95% interval
#>   informativeness I          0.157    0.000    0.570
#>   mean reliability           0.162    0.000    0.568
#>   dispersion H               0.0118   0.0000   0.0282
#>   concentration count J_eff  7.1      6.8      7.7      of 8
#>   logit variance V           0.230    (fixed by the standard errors)
#>   sigma_tau                  4.84     0.189    14.0
#>   effect mean                7.86     -1.27    17.1
#> 
#>   Pr(I > 0.5)                0.049
#>   I at E(sigma_tau^2)        0.203
